subject: print crashing (due to corruption of headers by #Adaptation terminated?)

messages.author: 7cc5dafb9f405296
messages.subject: print crashing (due to corruption of headers by #Adaptation terminated?)
parts:
Greetings,  I have a simple model with a fair amount of data producing a header line slightly more than 100,000 characters long which is truncated before all variables are written by # Adaptation terminated (without a preceding new-line).  Actually, the #Adaptation terminated is output in the midst of writing a variable, as in the following tail of that line ("It" does not occur in the model but variables beginning with "Item" do):
,It# Adaptation terminated

I suspect this causes print.exe (on Windows 7) to crash as follows:
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'boost::exception_detail::clone_impl<boost::exception_detail::error_info_injector<boost::bad_lexical_cast> >'
  what():  bad lexical cast: source type value could not be interpreted as target

Does this sound plausible and is this something I can fix on my end?  (Things otherwise work wonderfully.  Great software.)

Thanks, Paul

Which interface (RStan, CmdStan, PyStan, etc.)?

that it might cause a problem with buffer sizes.

Is there a way you can create a reproducible example we can
try out? We haven't had a problem like this reported before
that I recall.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] print crashing (due to corruption of headers by #Adaptation terminated?)
parts:
CmdStan. I'm working on a reproducible case but having trouble reducing
run-time below a day...

I guess that it's possible that this results from some inter-process
issue. The Stan executables are invoked from make which is invoked by a
controlling Java application which generates the model and/or data files
involved. Further, this occurred in the context of running that Java
application with the Eclipse IDE (with debugging). It also will not
surprise me if this a Windows-specific issue, whether with regard to
inter-process and/or buffered IO limitations that are less prevalent in
other operating systems (imo).

If I succeed in reproducing it in that environment I will then try it
from the command line directly and advise if there is a problem, perhaps
after trying it under Linux first. This will take a few days to complete.

Good to know such a thing is unprecedented.

Thanks,
Paul
